name: shop-serve~p1
task: Each time a client arrives, take their order, get food from the pantry, prepare it at the stove and hand it over; should the food fall, your very next move must pick it up.

value.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: the task's food-fall clause is a lasting condition paired with a one-step event: ChainResponse(food_fell, holding_food) can never be satisfied, because food_fell and holding_food never hold together ('food_fell and holding_food never hold together: the slip empties the hands'), so the very next step can never have holding_food true on the fall step's immediate successor while the fall is still pending as a ChainResponse — and an episode that ever ends on a fall goes to rejecting u14. Per the 'whenever a: do b, then c' rule, skip the lasting condition and link events: drop the food_fell clause (its pickup behavior cannot be expressed as ChainResponse over these propositions), or replace it with a Response(food_fell, ...) formulation; the three Response clauses for client_arrived->order_taken->food_prepared->order_served are correct.

CHANGES REQUIRED: 'should the food fall, your very next move must pick it up' is immediate-after wording, so it needs ChainResponse(food_fell, holding_food), but the candidate has Response(food_fell, holding_food). Response with a lasting condition (holding_food) never closes: it stays pending until holding_food happens at or after the fall, which also credits picking the food up many steps later or holding unrelated food. Replace the last clause with a hard ChainResponse(food_fell, holding_food). The three Response clauses for client_arrived -> order_taken -> food_prepared -> order_served correctly capture the per-client sequence and can stay.

CHANGES REQUIRED: the task states 'should the food fall, your very next move must pick it up', but no clause covers it. Add a hard ChainResponse(food_fell, holding_food) clause; keep the three Response clauses, which correctly capture the whenever-client pipeline (with the fetch-from-pantry step, a holding condition, correctly skipped in the chain).

NO CHANGES NEEDED: the task is a rule-only 'whenever' chain: Response(client_arrived, order_taken), Response(order_taken, food_prepared), Response(food_prepared, order_served) each capture one consecutive step of the serve routine, with no Existence demanded for condition events, and the food-fall clause is a lasting-condition note handled by the chain. Empty FINAL_STATES is valid here.

Each time an order is taken, food is prepared.
Each time food is prepared, the order is served.
